featured.title: India Is Hosting Iran, Russia, and China Under One Roof While American Missiles Hit the Gulf. Welcome to the BRICS Presidency.
featured.excerpt: As ministerial meetings stack up across Delhi and Nagpur ahead of September's summit, India's BRICS chairmanship is becoming a real-time test of Modi's diplomatic balancing act — with the diaspora's safety and prosperity on the line.
featured.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi at a BRICS Leaders' meeting in expanded format
featured.nri_angle: India's ability to maintain working relationships with both Washington and Tehran through the BRICS presidency directly determines the safety of nine million Indians in the Gulf, the stability of energy prices affecting diaspora families, and the remittance corridors that fund communities back home.
featured.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Is Hosting Iran, Russia, and China Under One Roof While American Missiles Hit the Gulf. Welcome to the BRICS Presidency.
news.excerpt: As ministerial meetings stack up across Delhi and Nagpur ahead of September's summit, India's BRICS chairmanship is becoming a real-time test of Modi's diplomatic balancing act — with the diaspora's safety and prosperity on the line.
news.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi at a BRICS Leaders' meeting in expanded format
news.nri_angle: India's ability to maintain working relationships with both Washington and Tehran through the BRICS presidency directly determines the safety of nine million Indians in the Gulf, the stability of energy prices affecting diaspora families, and the remittance corridors that fund communities back home.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: The Biggest Crackdown on Indian Crime in U.S. History Just Swept Three Continents. Here Is What It Means for the Diaspora.
news.excerpt: Operation Hard Ball charged 37 people tied to the Bishnoi and Bhagwanpuria gangs with racketeering, political assassination, and drug trafficking — and prosecutors say the investigation is far from over.
news.image_caption: The Robert F. Kennedy Department of Justice Building in Washington, D.C., headquarters of the federal prosecutors who led Operation Hard Ball
news.nri_angle: Indian American communities in California and across the U.S. were directly targeted by the syndicates through extortion, drug trafficking, and intimidation, making this the most significant law-enforcement action to confront transnational Indian organised crime on American soil.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: The European Parliament Just Condemned Pakistan for the Forced Conversion of Hindu and Christian Girls. The Numbers Are Staggering.
news.excerpt: Seventy-five per cent of forced conversion victims in Pakistan are Hindu. The EU resolution calls out a court ruling that validated the marriage of a 13-year-old Christian girl to her 30-year-old abductor.
news.image_caption: The European Parliament hemicycle in Strasbourg, France, where members voted on the resolution condemning forced conversions in Pakistan
news.nri_angle: Seventy-five per cent of Pakistan's forced conversion victims are Hindu — the EU resolution reinforces concerns held by the Indian diaspora and backs India's long-standing push for minority rights protection in Pakistan.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Lindsey Graham, the Senate's Loudest Voice on Iran and India, Dies at 71. His Empty Chair Changes the Calculus for Both.
news.excerpt: The South Carolina senator — Budget Committee chairman, immigration deal-maker, and the man who pressed Trump hardest on the Iran war now shaping life for nine million Indians in the Gulf — died of cardiac arrest Saturday night, a day after meeting Zelensky in Kyiv.
news.image_caption: Senator Lindsey Graham in his official 113th Congress portrait
news.nri_angle: Graham shaped key immigration policy including H-1B visa reform debates, championed the US-India defense partnership, and drove the Iran war policy now directly affecting nine million Indians in the Gulf — his absence shifts Senate dynamics on all three fronts.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Vance Just Launched the Biggest H-1B Fraud Probe in History. For 600,000 Indian Visa Holders, the Ground Just Shifted.
news.excerpt: The vice president's Milwaukee offensive targets not just visa cheats but the entire ecosystem Indian professionals navigate — from IT staffing firms to employment-based green cards. Immigration lawyers call it political theater. The diaspora is bracing for collateral damage.
news.image_caption: Vice President JD Vance, who announced the H-1B fraud investigation at a Milwaukee anti-fraud event on July 8, 2026.
news.image_credit: Official White House Photo by Emily J. Higgins, Public Domain, via Wikimedia Commons
news.nri_angle: With 73% of all H-1B workers coming from India, the Trump administration's fraud investigation creates existential anxiety across the Indian American professional class even as immigration lawyers insist actual fraud is rare.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: One Indian Crew Member Is Missing After Iran Attacked a Container Ship in the Strait of Hormuz. India Has Condemned the Strike.
news.excerpt: The GFS Galaxy was carrying 11 Indian nationals when Iran's IRGC Navy struck it Saturday, calling it a warning shot at an 'unauthorised' vessel. Ten Indians were rescued. The search for one continues.
news.image_caption: NASA MODIS satellite image of the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway between Iran and Oman where the GFS Galaxy was attacked
news.nri_angle: Indian seafarers face disproportionate risk as Iran-US war destabilises the Strait of Hormuz — one Indian crew member is missing and over 6,000 are stranded across the Gulf.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: An Indian Immigrant's Son Launches to the Space Station on Monday. He Spent a Year in India Vaccinating Children Against Polio.
news.excerpt: NASA astronaut Anil Menon — born to a Kerala-origin father and a Ukrainian mother in Minneapolis — lifts off aboard Soyuz MS-29 on July 14 for an eight-month mission. He is a Harvard neuroscientist, Stanford physician, former SpaceX flight surgeon, and the latest in a growing line of Indian-origin Americans reaching orbit.
news.image_caption: NASA astronaut Anil Menon in his official portrait at Johnson Space Center
news.nri_angle: Menon is the son of an Indian immigrant from Kerala and spent a formative year in India on a Rotary scholarship fighting polio — his launch is one of the most visible achievements by an Indian-American in the US space programme, following Kalpana Chawla, Sunita Williams, and Raja Chari.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Modi Signs a Strategic Partnership in Auckland. Outside the Arena, 300,000 Indian Kiwis Are Living Through a Racism Crisis.
news.excerpt: India and New Zealand elevated ties to a strategic partnership on Saturday — the first such visit by an Indian PM in 40 years — but the trade deal that brought Modi to Auckland has also unleashed a 'butter chicken tsunami' of anti-Indian backlash.
news.image_caption: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi during his three-nation Asia-Pacific tour
news.nri_angle: Modi's historic visit to New Zealand comes amid a surge in anti-Indian racism that has made the 292,000-strong Indian community a flashpoint in the country's immigration debate — a pattern disturbingly familiar to diaspora communities worldwide.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Six Thousand Seafarers Are Trapped in the Gulf. For Indian Sailors, the War Has Become Personal.
news.excerpt: Three Indian crew members are dead. One sailor watched 140 missiles fly in 30 minutes. Thousands more are stranded on ships running low on food and fuel. India is sending diplomats. The sailors want a way home.
news.image_caption: Satellite image of the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway between Iran and Oman where thousands of ships and seafarers remain stranded
news.nri_angle: Roughly 23,000 Indians work on merchant and offshore vessels in the Gulf region — India is one of the world's top three suppliers of seafarers, and the Iran war has killed three Indian crew members while trapping thousands more on ships under fire.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Just Sold Its Most Powerful Missile to a Third Country. The $630 Million Deal Rewrites the Indo-Pacific Arms Map.
news.excerpt: Indonesia becomes the third nation to buy the BrahMos supersonic cruise missile, after the Philippines and Vietnam. India's defence exports have grown thirty-five-fold in a decade.
news.image_caption: BrahMos supersonic cruise missile system on display during India's Republic Day parade in New Delhi
news.nri_angle: India's transformation from the world's largest arms importer to a meaningful defence exporter — with combat-proven systems now deployed across Southeast Asia — marks a generational shift in the country's global standing that NRIs have long advocated for.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: An Indian Immigrant's Son Just Entered One of America's Most Consequential Senate Races
news.excerpt: Dr Nirav Shah, who led Maine through COVID-19 and served as the CDC's second-in-command, is now running for Susan Collins's Senate seat. If he wins the nomination, he would be the first South Asian to run for Senate from New England.
news.image_caption: The Maine State House in Augusta, where Democrats are scrambling to name a Senate nominee
news.nri_angle: An Indian American — son of immigrants from India and former CDC deputy director — is now a leading candidate for the U.S. Senate in Maine, a test of South Asian political power at the highest level.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: The Iran War Just Went Gulf-Wide. For Nine Million Indians in the Region, the Fight Is Now Overhead.
news.excerpt: Iranian missiles struck targets in five Gulf states in a single day. The U.S. hit 300 targets in three nights. The Strait of Hormuz is closed again. And India's largest overseas community is caught in the middle.
news.image_caption: A U.S. Navy supply vessel transits the Strait of Hormuz, the strategic waterway through which one-fifth of the world's oil supply passes
news.nri_angle: Nine million Indians in the Gulf — the largest expatriate community in the region — are directly affected as Iranian strikes expand to five countries where they live and work, while 6,000 Indian seafarers remain stranded and Gulf remittances worth $28 billion face disruption.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Biggest Trade Deal Goes Live on Tuesday. Here's What Changes for the Diaspora in Britain.
news.excerpt: The India-UK free trade agreement enters force on July 15, cutting tariffs to near zero on 99 per cent of Indian exports, eliminating dual social security payments for 75,000 professionals, and creating mobility pathways for IT workers, chefs and musicians.
news.image_caption: India's Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal, who led the trade agreement negotiations
news.nri_angle: The 1.9 million Indians in Britain are directly affected: 75,000 professionals will stop paying double social security, 99% of Indian exports get duty-free access making Indian goods cheaper in UK shops, and 1,800 chefs, yoga instructors and musicians get dedicated work visas annually.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: An Indian American Congressman Was Detained at Gunpoint in the West Bank. He Says It Made Him More Likely to Run for President.
news.excerpt: Ro Khanna says armed Israeli settlers surrounded his van with M4 rifles, held his group for over an hour, and the IDF sided with the settlers — an experience he says strengthened his resolve to seek the White House in 2028.
news.image_caption: Ro Khanna, Democratic congressman from California, at a congressional hearing
news.nri_angle: Ro Khanna, one of the most prominent Indian American lawmakers in Congress, was detained by armed Israeli settlers while visiting the West Bank — an incident that has intensified his consideration of a 2028 presidential run and raised questions about Indian American political identity.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: The Supreme Court Just Saved Birthright Citizenship. For Half a Million Indian Families on Temporary Visas, It Was Never Abstract.
news.excerpt: A 6-3 ruling strikes down Trump's executive order denying automatic citizenship to children born to H-1B, H-4, and other temporary visa holders — preserving a right that quietly underpins Indian America.
news.image_caption: The United States Supreme Court building in Washington, D.C.
news.nri_angle: Over 5.4 million Indian Americans, most on temporary visas with decades-long green card waits, would have seen their U.S.-born children denied citizenship had the order stood.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Iran Just Closed the Strait of Hormuz 'Until Further Notice.' India Has Spent Four Months Preparing for Exactly This.
news.excerpt: A struck vessel, a formal closure, and a collapsing ceasefire — but India's petroleum minister says the country's crisis playbook has kept pumps open and prices lower than anywhere in the world.
news.image_caption: Satellite or aerial view of the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway through which a fifth of the world's oil once flowed
news.nri_angle: Six thousand Indian seafarers remain trapped in the Gulf, and the closure threatens India's fragile energy recovery — raising inflation, weakening the rupee, and straining supply lines that NRI remittances help sustain.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Goes Directly to Iran to Secure Passage for Nine Trapped Tankers and 198 Stranded Sailors
news.excerpt: With three Indian seafarers dead and an Indian supertanker forced to U-turn at Hormuz, the Modi government is opening its own diplomatic channel to Tehran — sidestepping a stalled American peace deal.
news.image_caption: An oil tanker docked at the Al Basrah Oil Terminal takes on crude in the Persian Gulf
news.nri_angle: Indian seafarers are dying in Gulf crossfire, oil prices threaten NRI household budgets worldwide, and India's LPG lifeline runs through the same choked strait.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Five Rules, One Target: The Trump Administration Is Rewriting Every Immigration Pathway Indians Use to Live in America
news.excerpt: H-1B placements face new scrutiny, Green Card wage floors are doubling, student visas will expire, and 100,000 H-4 spouses could lose work authorization — all by August.
news.image_caption: The United States Capitol at dusk in Washington, D.C.
news.nri_angle: The proposed rules collectively target every major immigration pathway used by Indian professionals, students, and families — H-1B, H-4, OPT, F-1, and Green Cards — with changes that could take effect within weeks.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: One Indian Sailor Missing, Ten Rescued After Iran Strikes Container Ship in the Strait of Hormuz
nri-world.excerpt: The attack on the GFS Galaxy is the fourth time in three months that a vessel with Indian crew has been hit in the Hormuz standoff. India's 300,000-strong seafaring community is running out of safe passage.
nri-world.image_caption: Naval vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz, where Indian-crewed commercial ships have repeatedly been struck since April 2026
nri-world.nri_angle: Indian seafarers — over 300,000 strong — are disproportionately exposed to the Hormuz standoff. Four ships with Indian crews have been struck since April. Maritime families in coastal India and across the diaspora live with a unique anxiety each time a vessel is hit.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: India's Tax Department Can Now See Your Foreign Bank Accounts. Here Is What Every NRI Needs to Know.
nri-world.excerpt: A CBDT order integrates overseas financial data from over a hundred countries into taxpayers' Annual Information Statements, closing one of the last gaps in cross-border tax visibility.
nri-world.image_caption: Aaykar Bhavan, the Income Tax Department's office in Pune, India
nri-world.nri_angle: NRIs with bank accounts, investments, or property in India now face unprecedented transparency — their overseas financial information from the US, UK, Canada, and other AEOI countries will appear in their Indian tax records, raising the compliance stakes for the 30-million-strong diaspora.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Anti-Sikh Hate Crimes Surged 3,700 Per Cent in a Decade. Anti-Hindu Incidents Hit a Record. The Numbers Keep Getting Worse.
nri-world.excerpt: FBI data for 2025 shows hate crimes against Sikhs, Hindus, and Buddhists reached their highest levels ever recorded, even as temples from California to Melbourne are being defaced with alarming regularity.
nri-world.image_caption: A Sikh gurdwara in the United States — anti-Sikh hate crimes have surged 3,700% over the last decade (Wikimedia Commons)
nri-world.nri_angle: For Indian Americans — especially Sikhs and Hindus whose faith is visually identifiable — the surge in hate crimes is reshaping daily decisions: whether to wear a turban to the grocery store, whether to let children walk to the gurdwara alone, and whether America still feels like home.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: The Billionaire, the Doctor, and the Toss-Up: Vivek Ramaswamy's Ohio Governor Race Just Got Real
nri-world.excerpt: Cook Political Report shifts the Ohio race from 'Lean Republican' to a dead heat. Polls show Ramaswamy and Democrat Amy Acton locked at 47-47 in a state Trump won by eight points.
nri-world.image_caption: Vivek Ramaswamy at a campaign event
nri-world.nri_angle: Ramaswamy's candidacy represents a new threshold for Indian American political ambition — a first-generation Indian American competing at parity in a major swing-state governor race, while the community's relationship with his brand of politics remains deeply divided.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: A Minister Called Them a 'Butter Chicken Tsunami.' A Preacher Threatened to Burn Their Temples. Then New Zealand Rolled Out the Red Carpet.
nri-world.excerpt: As Modi and Luxon elevated ties to a strategic partnership and 10,000 cheered at Auckland's Spark Arena, New Zealand's 300,000 Indians confronted a parallel reality — one defined by 4,767 hate incidents, death threats, and a political appetite for anti-migrant rhetoric.
nri-world.image_caption: The Auckland skyline, where PM Modi addressed Indian New Zealanders at the Kia Ora Modi event at Spark Arena
nri-world.nri_angle: New Zealand's 292,000-strong Indian diaspora faces the sharpest disconnect in the democratic world: courted as strategic partners at the state level while enduring the highest rate of racially motivated abuse in the country. The story maps the lived experience of Indians navigating hate crimes, political slurs, and temple threats in a nation that simultaneously seeks their trade, their talent, and their tourism dollars.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Six Months of America's Remittance Tax: The One Per Cent Levy That Rewired How the Diaspora Sends Money Home
nri-world.excerpt: What began as a five per cent scare in Congress ended up as a one per cent excise tax on certain transfers. Half a year into enforcement, the real effects are subtler — and more uneven — than either side predicted.
nri-world.image_caption: The United States Capitol in Washington, D.C., where the One Big Beautiful Bill Act was passed
nri-world.nri_angle: Every H-1B holder, green card carrier, and naturalised citizen who sends money to family in India now operates under this law. The exemptions favour those who bank digitally; the tax bites hardest on cash-and-counter senders — a distinction that splits the diaspora along class lines.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Five Thousand Visas, Working Holidays, and a Twenty-Billion-Dollar Promise. Inside the India–New Zealand FTA's Diaspora Dividend.
nri-world.excerpt: The landmark free-trade agreement signed in April and celebrated during Modi's Wellington visit this week contains the most NRI-friendly mobility provisions India has ever secured from a developed nation. A breakdown of what it means for professionals, students, and young Indians.
nri-world.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi with New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon. The two nations signed a landmark Free Trade Agreement in April 2026. (Photo: Government of India via Wikimedia Commons)
nri-world.nri_angle: This FTA is the most NRI-friendly mobility framework India has secured from a developed nation. The 5,000 skilled-worker visa quota, uncapped student admissions with extended post-study work rights, and 1,000 working-holiday visas create a structured pathway for Indians to live, work, and study in New Zealand — directly benefiting the 350,000-strong Indian Kiwi community and millions of prospective migrants.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Sunil Bharti Mittal Calls Indian Diaspora a 'Beautiful Bridge' as USISPF Honours Him with Leadership Award
nri-world.excerpt: The Bharti Enterprises founder was honoured alongside RTX's Christopher Calio and Fairfax Financial's V. Prem Watsa at the IX USISPF Leadership Summit in Washington.
nri-world.image_caption: Sunil Bharti Mittal at the USISPF Leadership Summit
nri-world.nri_angle: Mittal's speech directly celebrated the five-million-strong Indian diaspora in the US as the connective tissue between the two nations, with trade deal implications for NRI business leaders.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Seventy-One Per Cent Disapprove, Thirty-One Per Cent Have Gone Quiet on Social Media. Inside the Landmark Survey That Maps Indian America's Political Anxiety.
nri-world.excerpt: The Carnegie Endowment's 2026 Indian American Attitudes Survey of 1,000 adults reveals a community whose partisan loyalties are loosening, whose daily habits are shifting under the weight of discrimination — and whose frustration with American politics now outranks fear of racism as the reason some consider leaving.
nri-world.image_caption: A Diwali celebration in the United States — a landmark survey finds 71% of Indian Americans disapprove of the current political direction (Wikimedia Commons)
nri-world.nri_angle: The survey maps exactly how the 5.2-million-strong Indian American community is processing political volatility, online hate, and shifting identity — and how those forces are changing what they wear, where they travel, and whether they speak up in public.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: India Just Overhauled the OCI Card System for Five Million Holders Worldwide. Here Is What Changed — and What You Need to Do.
nri-world.excerpt: The Ministry of Home Affairs has introduced fully digital OCI applications, an electronic OCI card option, a $25 fine for non-compliance, and expanded eligibility — the biggest update to the programme since 2013.
nri-world.image_caption: An Overseas Citizen of India card — India has now introduced a digital e-OCI alternative alongside the physical document
nri-world.nri_angle: Every OCI holder abroad — from the tech worker in San Jose to the retiree in London — is affected by these rule changes. The new compliance requirements, especially the passport-update window and $25 fine, demand immediate attention from the diaspora.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Indian Banks Are Offering NRIs Up to Seven Per Cent on Dollar Deposits. The Window Closes in Eleven Weeks.
nri-world.excerpt: The RBI's special swap facility has removed the hedging cost that kept FCNR(B) rates stuck below four per cent. Indian Bank alone is targeting two billion dollars by September. Here is what NRIs need to know before the deadline.
nri-world.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai, which launched the special forex swap window for NRI deposits
nri-world.nri_angle: For NRIs parking idle dollars in US savings accounts yielding under one per cent, or even in Treasuries at four-and-a-half per cent, this is a rare moment when parking money in India carries no currency risk and pays meaningfully more — but only until September 30.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: From Tandoor to Michelin: Indian Fine Dining Is Conquering the World's Most Demanding Markets
nri-world.excerpt: A wave of Indian-origin restaurateurs and chefs — from the Sethi siblings in London to new outposts in Las Vegas, New York, and Dubai — is rewriting the global fine-dining map.
nri-world.image_caption: Indian fine dining has moved beyond the neighbourhood curry house, with restaurants like Gymkhana accumulating Michelin stars across London, Dubai, and beyond
nri-world.nri_angle: Indian-origin chefs and restaurateurs are leading the global expansion, reshaping perceptions of Indian cuisine and building cultural bridges through food.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: One in Five Ultra-Rich Indians Are Planning to Move Abroad — And It's Quietly Reshaping the NRI Financial Landscape
markets-finance.excerpt: A new Kotak Bank report reveals that 20% of India's ultra-high-net-worth individuals are migrating permanently while retaining citizenship, as India ranks third globally in millionaire outflows — behind China and the UK.
markets-finance.image_caption: Dubai Marina at night — the UAE has become the world's top destination for migrating millionaires
markets-finance.nri_angle: The Ultra-HNIs leaving India today are becoming tomorrow's NRIs — reshaping wealth management demand, FEMA compliance complexity, and cross-border financial infrastructure that all 32 million diaspora members navigate.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Indian Banks Race for Global Ratings as RBI's FCNR Dollar Drive Opens a Rare Window for NRI Depositors
markets-finance.excerpt: Federal Bank, YES Bank, and Bank of Baroda have secured international credit ratings to attract NRI deposits, while the RBI's special swap window offers up to 7.1% on dollar deposits — tax-free — until September 30.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRIs holding surplus dollars in low-yielding US savings accounts have a time-limited opportunity to earn 6-7% in dollar terms through FCNR(B) deposits at internationally rated Indian banks — tax-free under Indian law, fully repatriable. Window closes September 30, 2026.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: SEBI Wants to Double the Stocks You Can Short — And India's $5 Trillion Market Is About to Get a Lot More Interesting for NRIs
markets-finance.excerpt: India's market regulator is planning to nearly double stocks eligible for lending and borrowing from 176 to over 300, while cutting collateral from 130% to near-global levels — a move aimed at pulling retail investors away from the world's largest and riskiest derivatives market.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, India's oldest stock exchange
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors trading Indian equities through PIS accounts and GIFT City brokerages will benefit from deeper cash market liquidity and lower margin requirements, making hedging positions cheaper and more flexible
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: TCS Plans Up to 8,900 Forward-Deployed AI Engineers and Hunts for Acquisitions — What NRI Tech Investors Should Know
markets-finance.excerpt: India's largest IT firm is building an army of specialists who embed with clients to deploy AI, while eyeing its first major acquisitions in years. The strategy pits TCS against OpenAI and Anthropic, not just Infosys.
markets-finance.image_caption: A Tata Consultancy Services facility — TCS plans to deploy up to 8,900 AI engineers directly at client sites (Wikimedia Commons)
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI tech investors holding TCS — one of the most widely held Indian stocks in overseas portfolios — get mixed signals: the FDE strategy and acquisition appetite suggest AI as a growth engine, but decelerating AI revenue growth and a 32% share price decline in 2026 demand careful portfolio review.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's UPI Goes Global — Indonesia Integration, ECB Linkage, and a 20-Country Roadmap That Could Reshape How NRIs Move Money
markets-finance.excerpt: From Southeast Asia to Europe, India's payment rail is building cross-border corridors that could slash remittance costs and challenge Visa-Mastercard dominance — and the diaspora stands to benefit most.
markets-finance.image_caption: India's Unified Payments Interface logo — the payment rail now operates in eight countries and is targeting twenty by FY29 (Wikimedia Commons)
markets-finance.nri_angle: UPI's international expansion directly impacts NRIs through cheaper remittances, seamless travel payments, and new cross-border money corridors — potentially cutting transfer costs from 3-5% to under 1% on major diaspora corridors.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Goldman Sachs Upgrades Rupee Forecast to 94 — What NRIs Should Know Before the Remittance Window Closes
markets-finance.excerpt: The Wall Street bank sees the dollar-rupee pair plateauing as RBI measures, record bond inflows, and an unwind of rate-hike bets reshape the currency outlook. For NRIs, the 95+ remittance rate may not last.
markets-finance.image_caption: Indian rupee currency notes — NRIs face a narrowing window for favorable remittance rates
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRIs sending money home face a narrowing window: the rupee's current 95+ rate may tighten toward 94 if Goldman's forecast plays out. NRE deposit rates at 7%+ tax-free amplify the urgency.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Scraps Import Duties on Smartphone Parts and Lithium-Ion Cells — A $500 Billion Bet on Becoming the World's Electronics Factory
markets-finance.excerpt: New Delhi removes 5% and 7.5% levies on wireless charging modules, automotive displays, and battery cells in a move that benefits Apple and Xiaomi while targeting a 28-fold production growth encore by 2030.
markets-finance.image_caption: A printed circuit board — India's sweeping import duty cuts on electronics components aim to build a domestic manufacturing powerhouse
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors with exposure to Apple, Foxconn, Tata Electronics, and Indian EV battery plays stand to benefit as duty-free lithium-ion cell imports accelerate domestic manufacturing scale and attract fresh FDI into India's electronics corridor
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: SK Hynix's Record $26.5 Billion Nasdaq Debut Signals the AI Memory Supercycle Is Far From Over — Here's What NRI Tech Investors Should Know
markets-finance.excerpt: The South Korean chipmaker's largest-ever foreign listing on Wall Street — oversubscribed 7x, with shares surging 15% on day one — opens a new AI hardware play for diaspora investors already riding India's $2.6 billion TCS AI wave.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Nasdaq exchange in New York, where SK Hynix raised a record $26.5 billion in the largest U.S. IPO by a foreign company (Wikimedia Commons)
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI tech investors now have direct Nasdaq access to the AI memory chip boom through SK Hynix ADRs, complementing their India IT services exposure via TCS and Infosys. India's own semiconductor ambitions — Tata's Gujarat fab, Adani-Jabil AI infrastructure — position the diaspora to invest across the entire AI value chain from both sides of the Pacific.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's June Inflation Data Arrives Monday — CPI Expected to Breach 4% for the First Time in 16 Months, and NRI Portfolios Are in the Crosshairs
markets-finance.excerpt: A Reuters poll of 37 economists pegs June CPI at 4.3%, driven by food and fuel prices, El Niño fears, and Iran-war energy risks — with direct implications for RBI rate decisions, bond yields, and NRI deposit rates.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai, where monetary policy decisions shape NRI investment returns
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors with Indian fixed deposits, bond funds, and real estate exposure face a direct impact from the inflation print. A breach of 4% keeps deposit rates elevated but could halt the bond rally that foreign investors have been riding. Remittance values hinge on whether the rupee, currently at 95.32, holds or weakens on an inflation surprise.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Inc. Hedged a Record $120 Billion in June as the Rupee Swings Between War and Central Bank Muscle
markets-finance.excerpt: Corporate FX hedging hit an all-time high as the rupee whipsawed between 94.96 and 95.60 this week. Goldman Sachs sees the dollar-rupee at 94 in three months. Here's what the hedging boom means for NRI remittances.
markets-finance.image_caption: Indian rupee currency notes — the rupee traded between 94.96 and 95.60 this week amid geopolitical volatility
markets-finance.nri_angle: The rupee's trajectory directly affects every NRI sending money to India. With corporate hedging at record levels and Goldman Sachs forecasting USD/INR at 94 in three months (implying a stronger rupee), NRIs face a classic timing dilemma on remittances. The RBI's dollar-inflow measures could strengthen the rupee medium-term, meaning locking in today's 95+ rate for large transfers may be advantageous. NRE deposit rates, which are linked to rupee liquidity conditions, could also shift as RBI manages the inflow surge.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Shapoorji Pallonji Launches $650 Million Dollar Bond With BlackRock Backing — What NRI Investors Should Know About India's Hottest Debt Deal
markets-finance.excerpt: The Tata Sons-linked conglomerate's debut dollar bond at 14.5% yield has drawn Deutsche Bank as arranger and BlackRock as a likely investor, signalling growing global appetite for Indian high-yield corporate credit.
markets-finance.nri_angle: The deal signals maturing Indian corporate debt markets with yields far above NRE deposits — NRI investors can access this via global credit funds like BlackRock's Asia-focused vehicle, diversifying beyond traditional FD and equity exposure.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Silver Import Crackdown Sends Premiums to Six-Month High — What NRI Bullion Buyers Need to Know
markets-finance.excerpt: Imports have nearly halted after New Delhi hiked duties from 6% to 15% and restricted silver bars, grain, and powder. Domestic premiums have surged to $6.50 an ounce above global prices, and the squeeze is just getting started.
markets-finance.image_caption: Silver bullion bars — India's import restrictions have created acute domestic shortages
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRIs who buy silver bullion in India during visits, invest in Indian silver ETFs, or send money home for family jewellery purchases face a fundamentally different market. Premiums have flipped from discounts to double-digit surcharges, silver ETF outflows have released stored metal that is now drying up, and the import duty hike means any silver entering India costs 15% more at the border. For NRI investors holding Indian silver ETF units, the NAV may benefit from rising local premiums — but liquidity risk is growing as the physical market tightens.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Washington Is About to Rewrite the H-1B Playbook. Indian IT Giants Should Be Worried.
technology.excerpt: A sweeping regulatory package expected in August would tighten third-party placements, raise Green Card wage floors, and end open-ended student stays. For TCS, Infosys, and Wipro, the operating model itself is on trial.
technology.image_caption: The United States Capitol building at dusk in Washington, D.C.
technology.nri_angle: Indians account for 73 per cent of all approved H-1B petitions. The proposed rules directly target the third-party placement model used by Indian IT firms and would raise costs for Green Card sponsorship, restrict student work permits, and create gaps in spousal employment authorisation.

technology.title: India Wants AI Agents to Pay Your Bills. NPCI Is Building the Rails.

technology.image_caption: India's Unified Payments Interface (UPI) — NPCI is building a protocol to let AI agents make UPI payments autonomously
technology.nri_angle: UPI has become the payments layer NRIs encounter every time they visit India — and increasingly, when they send money home. If NPCI succeeds in building AI-agent infrastructure into UPI, it would position India's digital payments stack ahead of anything available in the US, where agentic commerce is still a collection of private initiatives by Visa, Google, and OpenAI.

lifestyle-health.title: South Asians Face Higher Heart Risk by 45 Despite Healthier Habits, Major Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A decade-long Northwestern study of 2,700 adults reveals a troubling paradox: South Asians report better diets and lower alcohol use but develop prediabetes and hypertension at double the rate of white Americans by midlife.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A blood pressure screening — a major new study finds South Asians face significantly higher cardiovascular risk by age 45 (Wikimedia Commons)
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asian Americans face uniquely elevated cardiovascular risk that standard BMI and lifestyle metrics fail to capture, demanding earlier screening and culturally tailored health interventions.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: India's Food Safety Regulator Just Called Out Dozens of 'Healthy' Brands. Here's Why NRIs Should Care.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: From Lotte's bread to Ferrero's Kinder Joy to Emami's cooking oil, FSSAI's unprecedented crackdown on misleading labels is exposing how some of India's most familiar packaged foods are not what they claim to be.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has issued notices to dozens of brands for misleading health claims (Wikimedia Commons)
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Many flagged brands — Emami, Lotte, Ferrero — are staples of NRI grocery shopping worldwide, and misleading 'healthy' labels on Indian packaged food directly affect diaspora consumers making dietary decisions.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Nita Ambani Receives Key to Tampa and Humanitarian Award as Indian-American Doctors Launch Cross-Border Health Alliance
lifestyle-health.excerpt: The AAPI convention drew over 2,000 physicians and unveiled targeted heart screenings for South Asians alongside a new India-America healthcare partnership

lifestyle-health.title: From Bhag Club to Bombay On Foot: How India's Run Club Boom Is Rewriting the Wellness Playbook

lifestyle-health.image_caption: Runners gather for an early morning group run in an Indian city park
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: NRIs watching India's community fitness explosion are finding parallels in their own cities — and many are launching or joining similar run clubs abroad, bridging diaspora loneliness with the Indian ethos of collective wellness.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The Science Is Settling: What 104 Clinical Trials Say About Turmeric's Real Health Benefits
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A sweeping meta-analysis of over 100 randomized controlled trials finds that curcumin supplementation significantly lowers blood sugar, cholesterol, and inflammation — but the dose and form matter more than your grandmother's golden milk recipe.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Fresh turmeric root and ground curcumin powder, staples of South Asian kitchens
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: For South Asians who grew up with turmeric as kitchen medicine, the largest-ever clinical review validates what their grandmothers always said — while revealing that traditional culinary doses and modern supplements are not the same thing.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Ayurveda Has Become a $20 Billion Global Industry. The Diaspora Is Still Figuring Out How to Feel About It.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: From ashwagandha gummies at Whole Foods to AI-powered dosha apps, India's ancient wellness traditions are everywhere — raising questions about appropriation, identity, and who profits
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Traditional Ayurvedic herbs and preparations that have found their way into mainstream Western wellness
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: NRIs watch their grandmothers' home remedies repackaged as premium Western wellness products — the $20B Ayurveda market raises urgent questions about cultural identity and who profits from Indian traditions
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: By 40, Half of South Asian Women in the UK May Develop a Chronic Disease, Landmark Study Warns
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A Queen Mary University study of 23,000 British Bangladeshi and Pakistani participants reveals that mental health and cardiovascular conditions cluster early — and the order they arrive in matters.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: The study, published in The Lancet, warns that half of South Asian women in the UK may develop a chronic disease by age 40 (Wikimedia Commons)
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asian diaspora communities in the UK, US, and Canada face elevated cardiovascular and mental health risks that begin a decade earlier than standard screening catches — this study argues for culturally tailored early intervention.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: India's Workers Are Losing 22 Days a Year to Extreme Heat. The Health Toll Is Even Worse.

lifestyle-health.image_caption: A construction worker in Kolkata — new research warns Indian workers will lose an average of 22.5 days annually to extreme heat (Wikimedia Commons)
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: NRIs whose families work in heat-exposed sectors face mounting health risks, and diaspora members visiting India during summer increasingly encounter dangerous conditions they are no longer acclimatised to.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Your Smartwatch Wasn't Built for You: Why South Asians Need to Rethink Wearable Health Data
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Wearable health devices are a $131 billion market, but their algorithms were trained on Western bodies — here is what diaspora Indians should actually track and why
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians face up to 4x higher cardiovascular risk yet wearable health algorithms are calibrated for Western populations — every NRI with a smartwatch needs to know what the numbers actually mean for them
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: Turmeric Is Officially 2026's Herb of the Year — Your Grandmother Knew Before Anyone
food.excerpt: The International Herb Association has crowned India's golden spice as the world's most important herb, capping a decade in which Ayurvedic staples went from immigrant kitchens to billion-dollar wellness aisles.
food.image_caption: Turmeric powder, named the 2026 Herb of the Year by the International Herb Association
food.nri_angle: The IHA designation validates what NRI families have known for generations — Indian spices are not folk remedies but scientifically validated health powerhouses, now driving a multibillion-dollar global wellness industry.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: India's Quiet Kitchen Takeover: Seven Indian-Chef-Led Restaurants Crack Asia's 50 Best Extended List
food.excerpt: From Mumbai's Papa's to Bangkok's Gaa, Indian culinary talent is showing up across Asia's most prestigious restaurant rankings — and the diaspora is eating well.
food.image_caption: A vegetarian thali showcasing the diversity of Indian regional cuisine
food.nri_angle: Nine Indian-chef-led restaurants across Asia's most prestigious rankings validate what the diaspora has long argued — Indian cuisine stands alongside any in the world.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: Patel Brothers, India Grocers, and the Quiet Empire Building of Indian Grocery in America
food.excerpt: From a 20,000-square-foot anchor store in Florida to a former Big Lots in Ohio, Indian grocery chains are expanding at a pace that mirrors the diaspora's own growth — and they are reshaping how America shops for food.
food.image_caption: An array of South Asian spices and ingredients on display at an Indian grocery store
food.nri_angle: Indian grocery expansion in suburban America is the infrastructure of belonging — when Patel Brothers opens in your suburb, it means home is a little closer.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: Dubai's Three-Michelin-Star Trèsind Lands in London — and Indian Fine Dining Will Never Be the Same
food.excerpt: Chef Himanshu Saini's celebrated Indian tasting-menu concept opens its first European outpost in Mayfair, marking a new milestone for Indian cuisine on the global stage.
food.image_caption: Indian fine dining is reshaping the global culinary landscape (Wikimedia Commons)
food.nri_angle: The first European outpost of the world's only three-Michelin-starred Indian restaurant rewrites the UK curry-house narrative for 1.8 million British Indians.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: From Amritsar's Bylanes to Harvard's Stage: Vikas Khanna Named Person of the Year
food.excerpt: Harvard's South Asian Association honors the Michelin-starred chef, filmmaker, and TIME 100 inductee — a crowning moment in a year that has redefined what Indian cuisine means on the world stage.
food.image_caption: Chef Vikas Khanna, the Michelin-starred chef and cultural ambassador honored by Harvard
food.nri_angle: Khanna's Harvard honor validates the cultural weight of Indian cuisine for NRIs who grew up seeing their food dismissed — now it is celebrated at the highest levels of American academia.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: From Gas Stations to Courtrooms: The Improbable American Life of Butter Chicken and Dal Makhani
food.excerpt: An Indianapolis food critic finds transcendent dal makhani behind a gas station's pizza warmer — while in Delhi, two restaurant dynasties battle in court over who invented it.
food.image_caption: A bowl of dal makhani, the creamy black-lentil dish at the center of an Indian culinary dynasty dispute
food.nri_angle: From gas-station deli containers in Indianapolis to $195 tasting menus in Manhattan, butter chicken and dal makhani bridge every chapter of the NRI experience.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

travel.title: Air India Cuts Flights to Chicago, San Francisco, and Toronto as Fuel Costs Bite
travel.excerpt: India's flag carrier has suspended Delhi-Chicago entirely and reduced frequencies on other key North American routes through August, leaving diaspora travellers scrambling for alternatives during peak summer.
travel.image_caption: An Air India Boeing 787-8 Dreamliner on the tarmac
travel.nri_angle: The Delhi-Chicago suspension and SFO/Toronto reductions directly hit NRI corridors — Chicago has one of America's largest Indian populations, and SFO serves the Bay Area's massive tech diaspora.
travel.author: Diaspora Desk

travel.title: Emirates Sends Its A380 to Delhi — and Premium Economy to Half of India
travel.excerpt: From October 25, the double-decker superjumbo joins Emirates' four daily Delhi services. Premium Economy will cover six Indian cities and nearly half the airline's India flights.
travel.image_caption: An Emirates Airbus A380-861 on the tarmac — the superjumbo will begin Delhi service from October 25
travel.nri_angle: Emirates is the go-to connecting airline for NRIs travelling between the US, UK, Canada, and India via Dubai. The A380 on Delhi and expanded Premium Economy across six cities means a materially better mid-cabin option on one of the most-flown diaspora corridors.
travel.author: Diaspora Desk

travel.title: LOT Polish Airlines Opens a New Delhi-to-Bay Area Route via Warsaw
travel.excerpt: A Boeing 787 Dreamliner connection through Warsaw Chopin Airport gives Indian travellers — and the Bay Area's large diaspora — another option on the India-US corridor.
travel.image_caption: A LOT Polish Airlines Boeing 787-8 Dreamliner — the aircraft type expected to serve the Delhi-Warsaw-San Francisco route
travel.nri_angle: The San Francisco Bay Area is home to one of the largest Indian diaspora communities in the US. A new Delhi-SFO routing via Warsaw adds competition to a corridor dominated by nonstops (Air India, United) and Middle Eastern hub connections, potentially pushing fares lower for NRI families making the trip home.
travel.author: Diaspora Desk

travel.title: Navi Mumbai Airport Gets Its First International Flight on Tuesday
travel.excerpt: Air India Express will fly twice weekly to Abu Dhabi from July 15, making Maharashtra's newest airport an international gateway — and giving Mumbai's eastern suburbs a far shorter ride to the Gulf.
travel.image_caption: Navi Mumbai International Airport terminal building in Maharashtra
travel.nri_angle: For NRIs from Navi Mumbai, Thane, and Pune — especially the large Maharashtrian and Gujarati diaspora in the Gulf — this eliminates the painful trek across Mumbai to Chhatrapati Shivaji airport.
travel.author: Diaspora Desk

travel.title: Georgia Is Europe's Best-Kept Secret for NRIs — and Your US Visa Gets You In
travel.excerpt: Indian visitor arrivals to Georgia surged 40% last year. Visa-free entry for US, UK, and Schengen visa holders, direct IndiGo flights from Delhi, and costs that undercut Western Europe by half are turning Tbilisi into a diaspora favourite.
travel.image_caption: Panoramic view of Tbilisi, Georgia's capital, with the Kura River and historic Old Town
travel.nri_angle: NRIs holding US, UK, or Schengen visas can enter Georgia visa-free for up to a year — no additional paperwork, no e-visa fees. Combined with IndiGo's nonstop Delhi-Tbilisi flights and costs 50-60% below Western Europe, it's an ideal short-break for diaspora families.
travel.author: Diaspora Desk

travel.title: Akasa Air Launches Direct Kochi-Kuwait Flights, Reopening Kerala's Gulf Lifeline
travel.excerpt: Starting August 1, the budget carrier will connect Cochin International Airport with Kuwait City, restoring a direct link that serves millions of Keralite expatriates in the Gulf.
travel.image_caption: Terminal 1 at Cochin International Airport, the departure point for Akasa Air's new Kuwait service
travel.nri_angle: Kerala's Gulf diaspora — estimated at over 2 million Malayalis across the GCC — depends on affordable direct flights between Kochi and Gulf capitals. The Akasa route fills a critical gap, particularly for blue-collar workers and middle-class families who can't afford premium carriers or long layovers.
travel.author: Diaspora Desk

travel.title: India's Passport Slips Two Spots — but 56 Doors Stay Open
travel.excerpt: The July 2026 Henley Passport Index nudges India down to 80th, though Indian travellers still enjoy visa-free or visa-on-arrival access to 56 destinations. For NRIs holding US or Schengen stamps, the real number is much higher.
travel.image_caption: India's e-Passport, introduced in 2024, now grants visa-free or visa-on-arrival access to 56 destinations
travel.nri_angle: NRIs with valid US visas or Schengen stamps unlock 30+ additional countries on top of the Indian passport's base list — making the practical travel footprint far larger than the headline ranking suggests.
travel.author: Diaspora Desk

travel.title: The NRI's Guide to Monsoon India — Where to Go, What to Skip, and Why July Is the Smartest Month to Visit
travel.excerpt: Domestic fares drop 30-50%, hotel rates crater, and India's most dramatic landscapes come alive. Here is how to plan a monsoon trip home that is memorable for the right reasons.
travel.image_caption: Houseboats on the Kerala backwaters — one of India's most stunning monsoon destinations (Wikimedia Commons)
travel.nri_angle: July and August are when most NRIs visit India — school breaks align, family obligations pile up, and the assumption is that monsoon means misery. In reality, it is the cheapest, least crowded, and most visually stunning time to travel the country.
travel.author: Diaspora Desk

travel.title: Jewar Airport Hits 48 Daily Flights — Just Four Weeks After Opening
travel.excerpt: Noida International Airport has quadrupled its flight count since its June 15 launch, now connecting 16 Indian cities. International services are expected later this year, giving NRIs a genuine alternative to the chaos of Delhi's IGI.
travel.image_caption: Prime Minister Modi at the inauguration of Noida International Airport at Jewar in March 2026
travel.nri_angle: For NRIs flying into Delhi-NCR to visit family in Noida, Greater Noida, Ghaziabad, or western UP — or heading onward to Agra and the Taj Mahal — Jewar could soon eliminate the two-hour slog across Delhi from IGI.
travel.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: Green Card Applicants Must Now Leave the Country. USCIS Calls It the Original Intent of the Law
carousel.excerpt: A policy memo reframing domestic adjustment of status as 'extraordinary relief' is the most fundamental change to the green card process in decades — and India's foreign minister has already raised the alarm with Washington.
carousel.image_caption: A USCIS Application Support Center in New York, where green card applicants have long filed adjustment of status paperwork
carousel.nri_angle: Hundreds of thousands of Indian H-1B holders in the employment-based green card pipeline now face the prospect of leaving the US to process at consulates booking 10-12 months out, upending the assumption that they could apply for permanent residence without disrupting their lives.
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: India Is Hosting Iran, Russia, and China Under One Roof While American Missiles Hit the Gulf. Welcome to the BRICS Presidency.
carousel.excerpt: As ministerial meetings stack up across Delhi and Nagpur ahead of September's summit, India's BRICS chairmanship is becoming a real-time test of Modi's diplomatic balancing act — with the diaspora's safety and prosperity on the line.
carousel.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi at a BRICS Leaders' meeting in expanded format
carousel.nri_angle: India's ability to maintain working relationships with both Washington and Tehran through the BRICS presidency directly determines the safety of nine million Indians in the Gulf, the stability of energy prices affecting diaspora families, and the remittance corridors that fund communities back home.
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: Dhamaal 4 Made ₹22 Crore on Saturday. Nobody Saw That Coming.
carousel.excerpt: A 64% jump from opening day, half a million BookMyShow tickets, and Ajay Devgn's biggest comedy weekend in years. The franchise just reminded Bollywood who really owns the multiplex.
carousel.image_caption: Ajay Devgn, who leads the Dhamaal franchise alongside Riteish Deshmukh and Arshad Warsi (Wikimedia Commons)
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: The Stage Is Set. Bellingham's England Meets Messi's Argentina in the World Cup's Defining Week.
carousel.excerpt: Saturday's quarterfinals delivered two extra-time thrillers in Miami and Kansas City. Now the last four convene in Dallas and Atlanta — and NRIs in those cities are already scrambling for tickets.
carousel.image_caption: Jude Bellingham celebrates after scoring for England at the 2026 World Cup
carousel.nri_angle: Both World Cup semifinals are in US cities with massive Indian-American populations — Dallas and Atlanta — making this a once-in-a-generation chance for NRIs to witness football's biggest stage in person.
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: Mercor Eyes $20 Billion Valuation as India's Invisible AI Workforce Powers Silicon Valley
carousel.excerpt: The AI data-labeling startup founded by Indian-American Adarsh Hiremath hit $2 billion in annual revenue — and its largest talent pool remains in India
carousel.image_caption: Data annotators labeling training data for AI systems at a labeling facility
carousel.image_credit: Nacho Kamenov & Humans in the Loop, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
carousel.nri_angle: Indian-American co-founder Adarsh Hiremath (Karnataka roots) built Mercor originally to connect Indian programmers to US companies; India remains the largest talent source for its 300,000+ expert contractor network; thousands of NRI professionals earn substantial incomes training AI remotely
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: One in Five Ultra-Rich Indians Are Planning to Move Abroad — And It's Quietly Reshaping the NRI Financial Landscape
carousel.excerpt: A new Kotak Bank report reveals that 20% of India's ultra-high-net-worth individuals are migrating permanently while retaining citizenship, as India ranks third globally in millionaire outflows — behind China and the UK.
carousel.image_caption: Dubai Marina at night — the UAE has become the world's top destination for migrating millionaires
carousel.nri_angle: The Ultra-HNIs leaving India today are becoming tomorrow's NRIs — reshaping wealth management demand, FEMA compliance complexity, and cross-border financial infrastructure that all 32 million diaspora members navigate.
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk
